text:
maria: quick question — if eu region is evicted and traffic falls back to us in an active/active fail, how do we prevent eu-resident PII tenants from being executed on a US quantized model? legal said cross-border execution for those tenants is a no-go.
ken: we must fail-closed for tagged tenants. otherwise we'll violate contracts.
devon: we have three high-level options: 1) keep standby capacity in eu and drain there, 2) route PII tenants to an eu-only hosted/dedicated pool, 3) return an explicit error and surface degraded behaviour to the app.
ashley: also callout: eu uses int8-q builds while us uses int4-q. numeric differences aside, legal's primary concern is data locality.
jon: proposal: enforce a residency routing policy in the edge proxy. policy checks tenant.residency tag and allows actions: reject with 503+explain, route to residency-only pool, or proxy to customer-managed in-region instance.
maria: is 503 acceptable from product POV? for top-tier high-sensitivity tenants product OK'd degradation for some SLAs but not all. need per-tenant policy.
ken: implementation principle: default best-effort for untagged tenants; fail-closed for tenants flagged "eu-pii". requires tenant metadata in auth token + enforcement in proxy.
devon: sketched logic for proxy rule: ```if tenant.residency == 'eu-pii' && current_region != 'eu': return 503, 'residency_fallback' elif current_region == 'eu': route_normal() else: route_best_effort_variant()```
ashley: ops note: during chaos/eviction tests we need metrics and traces to show how many requests were rejected vs routed. otherwise dashboards will show healthy QPS but with illegal execution.
jon: add metrics/resolution: residency.failover.rejected, residency.failover.routed; also add trace tag residency.failover=true + tenant_hash for audit.
ops-bot: chaos-svc: scheduled eu-region outage drill tomorrow 09:00 UTC. @ken @devon @ashley please be prepared.
ken: i'll add a canary asserting eu-pii tenants return 503, others route best-effort.
maria: cache/kv concern: we cannot hydrate eu-residency keys into us caches. that would move PII.
devon: proposal for cache behavior: mark residency-sensitive keys with residency tag and refuse cross-region hydrate. modes: copy(illegal), redirect(proxy back to eu kv), deny(return miss + degrade). default to redirect but legal may disallow reads.
ashley: checked with legal: cross-region read of ephemeral inputs is only allowed if data is pseudonymized. default must be deny unless tenant opts in. so default -> deny/hard-miss.
jon: next steps: i'll write an RFC follow-up to add tenant.residency_mode, cache residency enforcement, and a failover matrix mapping sensitivity -> allowed action. console should expose tenant-level residency policy toggle for admins.
maria: action items: jon -> RFC; devon -> PR for proxy rule & cache tagging; ken -> metrics + chaos canary; ashley -> update runbooks & confirm legal stance on cross-region reads. confirm by EOD.
ken: confirmed — i'll aim to have PR & canary by EOD. :thumbsup:
jon: rfc draft: https://rfc.internal/r/986-residency-failover (DRAFT) — feedback welcome.
maria: ack. during the chaos please triple-check that no eu-pii request is executed in us.
ops-bot: reminder: incident playbook "region-failover" v2.1 will be used for tomorrow's exercise.
